channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Janela Partidária: Podemos e PL saem vencedores; PDT e União perdem parte da bancada
item.description: The 2026 party window ended with significant gains for Podemos and PL, which increased their benches in the Chamber of Deputies. Podemos rose from 16 to 27 deputies, while PL grew from 87 to 97. Conversely, União Brasil and PDT suffered losses, reflecting strategic misalignments ahead of the October elections.

item.title: Partidos têm até esta quarta para indicar nomes para vaga de ministro no TCU, dizem líderes; entenda como funciona processo
item.description: Parties with representation in the Chamber of Deputies have until Wednesday (8) to nominate candidates for the TCU minister vacancy following the retirement of Aroldo Cedraz. The agreement between the government base and the PT to support Odair Cunha (PT-MG) remains in place, according to Chamber President Hugo Motta. Other parties have nominated Hugo Leal (PSD-RJ), Elmar Nascimento (União-BA), and Danilo Forte (PP-CE), while the PL is still deciding between Hélio Lopes (PL-RO) and Soraya Santos (PL-RJ).

item.title: Aposentadoria especial para agentes de saúde abre precedente descabido
item.description: The proposal for special retirement for health agents is deemed unfounded by experts, as it could create a R$ 29.5 billion deficit in the pension system over ten years, significantly impacting both the federal government and municipalities. Federal authorities and city halls are mobilizing to block the PEC in Congress, despite its growing support in an election year. The actual impact may be higher, as current estimates do not account for the revision of already granted pensions or the legal risk of other careers demanding similar benefits through the courts.

item.title: STF julga nesta quarta ações que discutem a eleição para o governo do Rio; entenda
item.description: The STF is ruling this Wednesday (8) on two actions regarding the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election, deciding between a direct (popular vote) or indirect (state deputies' vote) model. The election is needed due to a power vacuum following the resignation of Cláudio Castro and the disqualifications of Rodrigo Bacellar and Thiago Pampolha, leaving the state under the interim leadership of TJ-RJ president Ricardo Couto until 2027.

item.title: PL e Missão ganham mais filiados em ano eleitoral; MDB perde mais e PT também recua
item.description: The PL and the newly formed Missão party gained the most members in Brazil between January and March 2026, with the PL adding 43,588 affiliates and Missão gaining 7,820, driven by electoral mobilization for 2026. The MDB led in losses with 5,062 fewer members, followed by PRD, PP, and PT, which lost 3,215 members despite retaining a substantial base. Despite these shifts, the parties with the largest losses remain among the country’s biggest political formations, according to TSE data.

item.title: STF julga se eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio será direta ou indireta; entenda o que está em jogo
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court is ruling this Wednesday on whether the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial interim election will be direct (popular vote) or indirect (chosen by state deputies), following the resignation and electoral conviction of former governor Cláudio Castro by the TSE. The core issue is whether Castro’s resignation was electorally motivated — due to his conviction — which would invalidate the state’s indirect election law and trigger the federal Electoral Code, mandating a popular vote. Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Cristiano Zanin, Flávio Dino, and Gilmar Mendes have already advocated for direct elections, while the votes of Luiz Fux, Dias Toffoli, and Edson Fachin are expected to be decisive.

item.title: Gestão Nunes cobra de governo Lula decisão técnica sobre fim de contrato da Enel
item.description: The Aneel's decision to initiate the caducity process of Enel's contract was met with relief by Mayor Ricardo Nunes' administration, which views the move as a necessary technical step to ensure energy service quality in São Paulo. Nunes urged the Lula government to make a technical and impartial decision on terminating the contract, emphasizing the need to avoid political interference in regulatory matters.

item.title: Julgamento sobre eleições é novo capítulo de 'fator STF' na política do RJ
item.description: The Federal Supreme Court (STF) ruled on Wednesday (8) on the definition of Rio de Janeiro’s future interim governor, reinforcing the court’s role in state politics. The decision is seen as another chapter in the so-called 'STF factor,' which has increasingly influenced governance in the state.

item.title: Rede Sustentabilidade diz receber com 'indignação e perplexidade' anúncio da permanência de Marina Silva na sigla
item.description: The national leadership of Rede Sustentabilidade expressed 'indignation and perplexity' over Marina Silva's decision to remain in the party, after she refused to dialogue with the directory and accused her allies of practicing lawfare. The party denies having suggested her departure and asserts that allied exits resulted from collective democratic decisions, not persecution. Marina justified her stay as a commitment to Lula and Haddad's re-election and the strengthening of Brazil's 'democratic biome'.

item.title: Governo de SP quer criar Olimpíadas do Conhecimento
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has submitted a bill to the state legislature to institutionalize the Knowledge Olympics as a permanent program of the State Education Secretariat. Since 2024, the initiative has engaged over 4 million students and awarded 500,000 medals to top performers. The move aims to solidify the program as a lasting public education policy.

item.title: Confirmada eleição suplementar para a Prefeitura de Cabedelo (PB) no dia 12 de abril
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously upheld the removal of Cabedelo’s mayor André Luís Almeida Coutinho (Avante) and vice-mayor Camila Holanda (PP) for abuse of economic and political power and vote-buying. The decision confirms the supplementary election scheduled for April 12, after the regional court declared Coutinho ineligible for eight years and fined him R$ 40 thousand. The TSE dismissed their appeals, stating due process was respected and the evidence — including Pix transfers, food baskets, WhatsApp chats, and witness testimonies — was substantial.

item.title: TSE reconhece candidaturas fictícias nas Eleições 2022 para deputado federal em São Paulo
item.description: The TSE recognized that the Pros party launched two fictitious female candidacies in the 2022 federal deputy elections in São Paulo, but upheld the party's Drap because the valid female candidacies reached 36.61%, exceeding the 30% gender quota. Mariana Cristina Pontes Papaiz and Andrea Cristina Pradella had their candidacies annulled and were declared ineligible for eight years, while the party's proportional slate was preserved.

item.title: Mendonça é sorteado relator de queixa-crime de Bolsonaro contra Janones no STF
item.description: Justice André Mendonça was drawn as rapporteur for the criminal complaint filed by former President Jair Bolsonaro’s defense against Congressman André Janones, who is accused of slander and defamation based on videos from March calling Bolsonaro a 'vagabond,' 'thief,' and 'pervert,' among other allegations. This is Bolsonaro’s second private criminal action against Janones in the STF; Mendonça, appointed by Bolsonaro, had previously voted to dismiss the first complaint in 2024, but the Court followed Justice Cármen Lúcia and ruled Janones should stand trial for insult.

item.title: Ex-ministro Moreira Franco lança livro sobre bastidores da política
item.description: Former minister Moreira Franco will launch his book 'Politics as Destiny: Paths and Detours of Redemocratization' this Wednesday (8) in Brasília, gathering leaders from MDB and the centrão. The work addresses the trajectory of Brazilian redemocratization, focusing on political backstage dynamics.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro chama 'rachadinha' de espuma e diz que Queiroz tinha autonomia em gabinete
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) dismissed the 'rachadinha' investigations in his former Alerj office as 'foam', claiming they were an orchestrated attack to destroy his reputation. He asserted that former aide Fabrício Queiroz had autonomy in the office and that the allegations lack substance.

item.title: Câmara aprova regras para transição de governo e prevê punição por omissão de dados
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill establishing rules for the presidential transition after elections, setting deadlines, obligations for data and document sharing, and penalties for non-compliance. The text requires the transition team to be named within 72 hours of the election result proclamation and mandates the outgoing government to facilitate access to systems, contracts, and civil servants. The bill now proceeds to the Chamber’s Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) and then to the Senate.

item.title: Câmara aprova projeto que estabelece regras para a transição entre governos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill establishing mandatory rules for the administrative transition between governments following the proclamation of election results. The legislation aims to ensure continuity of public services and information exchange between outgoing and incoming teams, with set deadlines for document delivery and management reports.

item.title: Caiado minimiza elo de PSD com Lula após janela partidária e diz ter palanque garantido
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, former governor of Goiás and PSD's pre-candidate for president, downplayed the entry of Lula-aligned parliamentarians into his party following the partisan window, stating it would not impact his campaign. He asserted he has a solid Northeastern electoral base that, he said, 'will surprise' opponents.

item.title: PL trabalho por aplicativos: relator mantém mínimo de R$ 8,50 por entrega e prevê piso de R$ 14,74 por hora trabalhada
item.description: The rapporteur of the app-based work regulation bill in the Chamber of Deputies, Augusto Coutinho, established two minimum pay options for delivery workers: R$ 8,50 per delivery (up to 3km by car or 4km on foot/bicycle/motorcycle) or R$ 14,74 per hour worked (equivalent to two minimum wages). The text does not create an employment relationship but guarantees rights such as social security, accident insurance, transparency in suspensions, and a 30% cap on platform retention for passenger trips.

item.title: Lurian Lula relembra 8 anos da prisão do pai: “A verdade venceu”
item.description: Lurian Lula recalled the 8th anniversary of her father Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s imprisonment on April 7, 2018, emphasizing the family’s emotional struggle, weekly visits to Curitiba, and his resilience during 580 days in jail. She described a role reversal in emotional support and celebrated the 2021 Supreme Court annulment of his convictions, which restored his political rights and enabled his 2022 election victory, concluding with 'The truth prevailed'.

item.title: “É o PL que faz oposição ao governo Lula”, afirma Sergio Moro
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro explained that he left União Brasil to join the Liberal Party (PL) because it is the PL that effectively opposes President Lula’s government. He added that the PL gave him freedom to assemble his political team, reinforcing his pre-candidacy for governor of Paraná in 2026.

item.title: Governistas da CPMI do INSS entregam relatório alternativo à PF
item.description: Government-aligned members of the INSS CPMI delivered an alternative report to the Federal Police, CGU, and MPF, proposing the indictment of 130 individuals, including former President Jair Bolsonaro, his son Flávio, Daniel Vorcaro, and Onyx Lorenzoni, over alleged involvement in illegal discount schemes in social security benefits. The report, previously rejected by the majority, was presented as a counter to the rapporteur Alfredo Gaspar’s (União-AL) report, which included Fábio Luís Lula da Silva. CPMI President Carlos Viana was accused of sabotaging the process by refusing to put the report to a vote.

item.title: Relator mantém mínimo de R$ 8,50 para entregadores e altera regras de contribuição e seguro em projeto de trabalho por app
item.description: Relator Augusto Coutinho maintains the R$ 8.50 minimum payment for delivery workers in his report on the app-based work bill, rejecting the Lula government’s proposal to raise it. The text includes a 5% social security contribution for workers and 20% for platforms (or 5% of gross revenue), requires personal accident insurance with a minimum coverage of R$ 120,000 adjusted annually by IPCA, and allows platforms to charge up to 30% of the order value as a service fee. Despite the changes, the report is expected to gain government base support, with allies proposing only amendments suggesting a R$ 10 minimum per order.

item.title: TSE realiza nesta quinta (9) atualizações na infraestrutura de Tecnologia da Informação
item.description: The TSE will perform IT infrastructure updates from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM this Thursday (9) to enhance security and performance of the ELO and ODIN3 systems, possibly causing temporary service unavailability. Users can access systems directly via their corresponding addresses to avoid re-authentication after the update.

item.title: Câmara aprova regras para a transição de governos entre a eleição e a posse
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved Bill 396/07, establishing minimum rules for government transition between election and inauguration, requiring the outgoing administration to facilitate access to information, facilities, and technical support for the incoming government. The bill includes administrative and legal sanctions for non-compliance, including fines and liability for damages, with increased penalties for deliberate data destruction, asset damage, or intimidation of officials. The transition team must be formed within 72 hours in equal representation from both sides.

item.title: Kassab projeta Caiado com 15% dos votos e cita poder de barganha no 2º turno: 'Vamos apoiar porque queremos isso e isso'
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, stated that achieving 15% of the vote in the first round would be 'excellent' for Ronaldo Caiado, as it would provide bargaining power in a potential runoff. He emphasized the need for an alternative candidacy given the high rejection of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, noting the party has three months to reach 10% in polls by end of June. Caiado described the 15% target as a 'takeoff' and positioned his campaign around delivery, respect, and results, rejecting polarization.

item.title: Caiado se muda para SP, mira eleitor 'desiludido' e busca vice que torne chapa mais competitiva
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD's pre-candidate for Presidency, moved to São Paulo after resigning as governor of Goiás to position himself in the country's largest electoral college. His initial strategy is to present his political and gubernatorial experience to 'disillusioned' voters weary of polarization, offering himself as an alternative to Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. He promises broad amnesty for those involved in the January 8 events as his first act and seeks a running mate who can add votes and TV time, while citing his 88% state approval rating as evidence of his dialogic approach.

item.title: Fim da 6x1 no Congresso: Planalto contradiz Motta e diz que estuda urgência para projeto
item.description: The Planalto contradicts House Speaker Hugo Motta’s claim that the government has abandoned sending an urgent bill to end the 6x1 work schedule. The government says Ministers Sidônio Palmeira and Guilherme Boulos are still evaluating the bill’s submission to Congress, while Motta states the Executive prefers advancing the proposal via a Constitutional Amendment (PEC), currently under review in the CCJ.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Governo contradiz Motta e nega ter desistido de enviar projeto que reduz jornada
item.description: The Lula government denied abandoning plans to send a bill to Congress ending the 6x1 work scale, contradicting statements by House Speaker Hugo Motta. Ministers Guilherme Boulos and Sidônio Palmeira said the Executive remains committed to sending the proposal, which calls for a 40-hour workweek with two days off and no salary reduction, possibly under urgency regime. The text is expected to be finalized in upcoming meetings.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: A paz selada entre André Marinho e o clã Bolsonaro
item.description: André Marinho, pre-candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, publicly sealed an alliance with the Bolsonaro clan on the show 'Papo Antagonista', emphasizing their joint opposition to Lula's re-election in 2026. The meeting, shared in a video on social media, underscores the opposition's effort to consolidate support behind an alternative candidate to the federal government.

item.title: André Mendonça será o relator de queixa-crime de Bolsonaro contra Janones
item.description: Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça was randomly assigned as rapporteur for the criminal complaint filed by former President Bolsonaro against deputy André Janones for slander, libel, and defamation. Mendonça, appointed by Bolsonaro and known for lenient votes toward January 8 rioters, now oversees the case after handling the INSS and Master scandals. The rapporteur sets the procedural schedule, requests hearing dates, and votes first in the Court.

item.title: Governo Lula quer manter PL da 6 X 1 sem regra de transição
item.description: The Lula government maintains its intention to send to Congress a constitutional urgency bill to end the 6x1 work schedule, establishing a 40-hour weekly wage, maintained salaries, and two days off per week, without transition rules. Despite House Speaker Hugo Motta claiming the bill was abandoned and would proceed as a PEC, the Planalto Palace denies suspension and states meetings are scheduled to set the submission date, aiming to preserve executive leadership on the agenda. The proposal contrasts with others, such as that of Deputy Erika Hilton, which advocate gradual adoption to reduce labor market impacts.

item.title: Caiado rebate Kassab e promete estar no segundo turno
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado rebutted PSD president Gilberto Kassab's claim that 15% of the vote would be an 'excellent' result for the party's presidential candidacy, calling the figure 'a takeoff, a beginning of discussion'. Caiado promised to be in the runoff of the 2026 presidential elections, asserting that his political project has the potential to grow beyond initial expectations.

item.title: Datafolha: os dois principais fatores em jogo na nova pesquisa sobre Lula x Flávio
item.description: The new Datafolha poll, conducted after Ronaldo Caiado’s official pre-candidacy announcement and the initial effects of Lula’s fuel policies, is highly anticipated for capturing the combined impact of these two developments on the electoral landscape. It may reveal vote shifts, particularly among 'third way' voters, and indicate whether there is a meaningful impact on the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The results are expected to highlight trends — not just raw numbers — such as electorate reactions to recent political movements.

item.title: Motta prevê avanço da PEC da escala 6×1, do trabalho por apps e da escolha para o TCU
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced that the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule will have its admissibility report voted next week in the CCJ, followed by the creation of a special committee to discuss the text with the goal of bringing it to the plenary by the end of May. He also stated that the Chamber aims to advance the bill regulating work for app-based workers, with a new version of the rapporteur’s opinion to be presented this Wednesday and a possible vote in the special committee next week, aiming to provide social security, health and life insurance for over 2 million workers.

item.title: Cleitinho critica STF por julgamento sobre o 8 de janeiro
item.description: Senator Cleitinho (Republicanos-MG) criticized the STF for sentencing businessman Alcides Hahn to 14 years in prison for financing transportation to the January 8, 2023 riots, questioning the Court's consistency when it rules on the future plea bargain of Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, and calling for votes on impeachment petitions against justices. He also supported ending the 6x1 work schedule, arguing the government should bear the cost since entrepreneurs and workers create wealth, and demanded spending cuts across the three branches and an end to pensions for military daughters.

item.title: TSE rejeita cancelar o registro do PL por submissão aos EUA
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) rejected a request to cancel the registration of the Liberal Party (PL), filed by two voters who alleged the party is subordinated to the U.S. government. The Court declined to rule on the merits, citing Brazilian electoral law, which restricts such actions to parties or the Electoral Public Ministry (MPE). Minister Isabel Gallotti had previously dismissed the case based on the PGE’s opinion, which found no sufficient evidence to support the claim of PL’s submission to the White House.

item.title: Relator confirma o fim da CPI do Crime Organizado e critica Alcolumbre
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE), rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI, confirmed the committee will not be extended after a meeting with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who cited electoral year risks. Vieira criticized Alcolumbre for delivering a 'great disservice' and stated he will not appeal to the STF, respecting existing jurisprudence, despite opposing the premature closure.

item.title: Senado reconhece estágio como experiência profissional
item.description: The Senate approved Bill 2762/2019, which establishes that internships completed by students will count as professional experience, amending the 2008 Internship Law. The proposal now heads to presidential sanction and aims to reduce the barrier of lack of experience for young people aged 18 to 24 in the job market. Additionally, bills were passed allowing health residents to split their annual 30-day leave into periods of at least 10 days and establishing a Mixed Parliamentary Front in Defense of Street Vendors.

item.title: Os cenários para o julgamento das eleições para mandato-tampão no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) is set to rule on April 8 on whether Rio de Janeiro’s interim governor election will be direct or indirect, with ministers divided on whether Cláudio Castro’s resignation one day before his electoral crime conviction was fraud or a legal strategy. Minister Cármen Lúcia supports indirect elections with a 24-hour incompatibilization period, while Alexandre de Moraes, Flávio Dino, Cristiano Zanin, and Gilmar Mendes favor direct elections, viewing the resignation as a fraud to prevent political loss. Eduardo Paes’s PSD party contests the TSE’s directive for indirect elections, arguing it undermines their ability to run in both the interim and general elections.

item.title: Indústria do fumo critica alta do IPI sobre cigarros
item.description: The Brazilian Tobacco Industry Association (Abifumo) criticized the government's increase in the IPI tax on cigarettes, announced by President Lula's administration, stating it 'triggers a critical alert' for the economy and public safety. The association argues the tax hike could negatively impact the sector and lead to social consequences.

item.title: Nunes cobra celeridade do governo após decisão da Aneel: 'Estamos exaustos'
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) urged the federal government to act swiftly in declaring the Enel contract forfeit following a unanimous decision by Aneel’s technical body to deny renewal of the company’s electricity concession in the city. He said residents are 'exhausted' by recurring power supply issues.

item.title: Caiado volta a criticar polarização e comenta fala de Kassab sobre 'meta' de 15% de votos: 'arrancada'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD's presidential pre-candidate, criticized Brazil's political polarization between Lula and Bolsonaro and said Gilberto Kassab's suggested 15% vote target is merely a 'starting point' for discussion. He asserted he will surpass that, reach the runoff, defeat Lula, and govern based on results, experience, and dialogue — rejecting the culture of likes and insults. Caiado also contrasted his political experience with Flávio Bolsonaro's, likening it to choosing an experienced surgeon over a novice.

item.title: Mendonça é sorteado para relatar ação de Bolsonaro contra Janones
item.description: Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça has been randomly assigned as rapporteur of a criminal complaint filed by Jair Bolsonaro against federal deputy André Janones. The case stems from Janones’ remarks calling Bolsonaro a 'thief' and 'vagabond', and accusing him of ordering the killing of Lula and Alckmin. Bolsonaro’s defense seeks conviction for slander, defamation, and insult, plus moral damages compensation.

item.title: 'É guerra, não ganância': o que ameaça o pacote de Lula para segurar o preço do diesel
item.description: The Lula government announced an expanded subsidy package to curb diesel price increases, aiming to prevent further economic and political impacts, especially in light of the 2018 truckers' strike. Measures include higher subsidies for domestic producers and greater discounts for imported diesel in participating states, though experts warn the effect will be limited due to international uncertainty and resistance from major fuel companies to join the program.

item.title: “Na prática, é uma intervenção política”: demissão na Petrobras acende alerta no mercado
item.description: The federal government attempted to curb rising fuel and cooking gas prices through tax exemptions, subsidies, and state-level coordination, but the dismissal of a Petrobras director following a high-premium gas auction was seen as political interference, raising concerns about the company's autonomy, governance, and market confidence.

item.title: Governo desistiu de enviar PL próprio sobre fim da 6 X 1, diz Motta
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies Hugo Motta announced that the Lula government has withdrawn its plan to send a constitutional urgency bill on ending the 6×1 work scale, opting instead to await the PEC on the matter. The PEC will be voted on in the CCJ next week, and if approved, a special committee will be immediately established to discuss reducing the workday, with a vote expected in May before the elections.

item.title: A projeção de Kassab sobre o desempenho de Caiado na eleição
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, stated that 15% of votes for pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado would be 'great', even if it doesn't lead to a runoff, emphasizing the importance of a political alternative. He noted that such a vote share would allow the party to negotiate support in exchange for specific policy demands. The projection comes ahead of the release of a new Ideia poll with 1,500 interviews and a 2.5-point margin of error.

item.title: Indígenas pedem maior proteção às suas terras durante marcha em Brasília
item.description: Thousands of indigenous people from across the country marched in Brasília to demand faster demarcation of indigenous lands by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government and to protest against Congress, six months ahead of the elections in which Lula seeks re-election.

item.title: Em ritmo de pré-campanha, marqueteiro de Lula diz a deputados do PT para reforçar presença digital
item.description: Raul Rabelo, marketing strategist and partner of Communications Minister Sidônio Palmeira, presented initial campaign strategies for Lula’s 2026 re-election bid to the PT caucus in the Chamber of Deputees, stressing the need to strengthen digital presence through social media, supporter accounts, and influencers. The 26-slide presentation highlighted themes such as ending the 6x1 work schedule, combating family debt, and contrasting Lula’s legacy with Bolsonaro’s, while noting that the 'blusinhas' tax is the most unpopular measure of Lula’s government, opposed by 70% of Brazilians. Rabelo urged the campaign to portray Lula as aligned with workers and the most vulnerable.
